title: Ben Johnson: Players are ‘fighting to be on that grass and help us win’ | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams is not practicing Saturday and Chicago is leaving the Monday night QB order open. Tyson Bagent is cleared from concussion protocol and back at practice, with Case Keenum the other option.
summary: Johnson said the week has gone well, but active and inactive decisions for Monday night are still uncertain, so the team will let the practice process play out. Caleb Williams will not practice Saturday, and no reason was given in this transcript. Tyson Bagent is back at practice after clearing concussion protocol and was in meetings Friday. Johnson said he needs to see something from everybody today. Asked about the QB pecking order, Johnson said the plan is to finish the week as planned and then decide. He noted Bagent was the backup coming out of camp and that he and Keenum have different skill sets (one is more mobile, both are cerebral). He also said Bagent could be the backup Monday. Johnson praised Keenum, whom he recruited as a potential third QB, and said big things are expected if Keenum plays. Kicker Cairo Santos is practicing and the team added no extra kicker. Ozzy Trapilo is not expected to play Monday in any capacity. A call about the kickoff discrepancy is expected Saturday afternoon.

injuries.detail: Will not practice Saturday. No reason or Monday outlook was given in this transcript.
Cleared concussion protocol, in meetings Friday and back at practice Saturday. Johnson wants to see how he looks.
Asked whether he would play in any capacity Monday, Johnson answered 'No.'

signals.claim: Williams will not practice Saturday; his Monday availability was not confirmed.
signals.note: A missed final practice with no stated reason puts his Monday night status in doubt, so have a fallback plan.
signals.quote: Caleb, uh, will not be practicing today.

signals.claim: Bagent could be the starter or the backup Monday night, depending on a staff decision after Saturday's practice.
signals.note: He is cleared from concussion protocol, was the backup coming out of camp, and could be the QB Monday if Williams is out.
signals.quote: there's a reason why Tyson was the backup as we ended camp.

signals.claim: Keenum may play Monday night, and the staff has not set the QB order yet.
signals.note: He has taken more practice snaps than Bagent this week, so he is a live option if Williams can't go.
signals.quote: if he plays Monday night, you know, we're, uh, we're expecting big things from him.

signals.claim: Trapilo will not play in any capacity Monday night.
signals.note: His absence thins the offensive line, which matters for the run game and QB protection.

topics.detail: Cairo Santos is practicing Saturday. Johnson said the team felt good about where he was and signed no extra kicker, only having contingency plans.
Johnson understood there was a call Saturday afternoon to settle the kickoff controversy or discrepancy, but he wasn't sure of the details.
Johnson will finish the week as planned, then decide as a staff on the QB order. Both quarterbacks are described as cerebral, with Bagent less mobile in contrast to Keenum or vice versa in skill set.
Johnson doesn't focus on the time slot. The team prepared in a 'chaotic by design' way in camp, and he expects a charged home crowd.

title: Exclusive: Kellen Moore previews Saints' home opener vs. Raiders
headline: Saints open at home vs. undefeated Raiders with Asim Richards filling in for injured Kelvin Banks at tackle; Moore stressed quick passes and protection against a sack-heavy Raiders front.
summary: Moore said the team is excited for its first regular-season home game in the Superdome, citing the crowd and atmosphere as an advantage that the team has to earn by playing well. He called the undefeated Raiders tremendously talented, noting their front four rushes well and their pressure packages are strong, and said the Saints must be aware of it. His plan is to get the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly and execute blocks when protection is needed. With Kelvin Banks out of the lineup, Moore expressed confidence in Asim Richards, who got opportunities last year and played well at Baltimore against a tough defense. Richards will get a full week of preparation as the starter. Moore also praised Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins as steady and calm, saying teammates play better around him. No other injury or skill-position news was shared.

injuries.detail: Implied to be unavailable this week since Asim Richards is stepping in for him; the specific injury and status were not given.

signals.claim: Will start in place of Kelvin Banks against the Raiders after a full week of preparation.
signals.note: Richards' pass protection against a sack-heavy Raiders front matters for Tyler Shough and the Saints' passing game.

signals.claim: Saints will aim to get the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly against the Raiders' pass rush.
signals.note: A short, quick passing game against heavy pressure could limit downfield aggressiveness and raise sack risk with a backup tackle.
signals.quote: We've got to get the ball out of our hands

topics.detail: The Saints return to the Superdome for their first regular-season home game; Moore emphasized that the team must play well to energize the crowd.
Las Vegas is tied for the league lead in sacks and gets pressure from its front four plus blitz packages; the Saints need awareness, quick throws, and sound blocking.
Moore described Cousins as a steady, calm presence who lifts the play of those around him, helping Las Vegas start 2-0.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 26, 2026
headline: Sirianni says Makai Lemon's touches will come but stays non-committal on feeding him; Zach Ertz and Kenny Moore II are ramping up with good weeks, and their game status will be decided after the final practice.
summary: Sirianni sidestepped a question about the special teams controversy over using a 12th man on kickoffs, saying the Eagles operate within the rules and will do what gives them the best chance to win. He said the team had a good week of practice, singled out the tight ends and Zach Ertz as having good weeks, and said they would see where things stand at the end of the day. On Makai Lemon, he said the rookie is improving each week and doing things the stat sheet does not show, and that his touches will come. He also said DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (referred to as Smitty and Tay) have started the season well. He explained that Ertz and Kenny Moore II, who missed training camp, are being evaluated by how they move and feel after practice and by how well they pick up the system. He praised Jalen Hurts and defended the low play-action rate as a small sample size affected by no-huddle work and being behind the sticks. He said a returning player, apparently Ertz, is still limited but had a good week and brings good energy and leadership. He also said the center and left guard combination had a good week of preparation in new spots. The team travels to Chicago for Monday Night Football.

injuries.detail: Still limited in practice but had a good week and is ramping up after missing training camp. Game status will be assessed after the final practice.
Being ramped up after missing training camp and is learning the system. Sirianni said readiness varies by player and the team is checking how he looks and feels after each practice.

signals.claim: Lemon's touches will increase over time as he continues to do the right things when the ball is not going to him.
signals.note: Lemon is not yet a priority target in a crowded passing offense, so his fantasy role depends on patience rather than an imminent target bump.

signals.claim: Ertz is trending toward playing after a good week of practice, with a final decision after the last practice.
signals.note: A returning Ertz could take targets at tight end, and a good practice week suggests he is close to playing.
signals.quote: he's had a good week. It brings good energy.

signals.claim: Smith will remain a main target in the passing game given his good start to the season.
signals.note: Sirianni named Smith as a primary beneficiary of the passing volume, and his role looks secure.
signals.quote: I think Smitty and Tay have had a good start to the season

signals.claim: Wicks, referred to as Tay, will continue to be a main target after a good start to the season.
signals.note: He is named alongside Smith as producing, which supports his fantasy value as a pass catcher.
signals.quote: I think Smitty and Tay have had a good start to the season

signals.claim: Play action will likely increase as the offense settles into its identity, though the current usage is low.
signals.note: Hurts is praised for handling play action well, but the low rate shows a small sample and the offense is still finding itself.
signals.quote: it gives Jalen really good space from the line of scrimmage

topics.detail: Sirianni did not give a direct resolution on using a 12th man on kickoffs. He said the Eagles are within the rules and will do what gives them the best chance to win.

Drew Kendall at center and a teammate at left guard (likely Cam Jurgens' replacement) had another full week of practice in new spots. Sirianni said the preparation has been good but guarantees nothing.
Sirianni said the low play-action rate comes from a small sample, no-huddle work, and being behind the sticks. He said the team is still figuring out who it is and what it does best.

Sirianni said there is no checklist for ramping players up. The staff watches movement, how players feel after practice, how well they learn the system, and habits like tackling and protecting the ball.
